comparator.name: Information Science (Informatiekunde)
comparator.sourceNotes: Appendix D, Articles 3.6–3.7 and Tables 1.1–1.3 define a 135 EC major and 45 EC of profiling electives. The major includes ten compulsory 7.5 EC courses, one 30 EC study path, 15 EC of other major electives and a compulsory individual 15 EC research project. The example uses Informatiesystemen and the first two eligible additional electives, Cognitie en emotie and Usability engineering en user experience. The research project requires 120 EC and completion of Wetenschappelijke onderzoeksmethoden. Profiling must include at least 15 EC at level 2 or 3 and avoid overlap. The example reaches 45 EC at level 3 within the major. The two tutorials carry zero credits.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target is the generic Informatiekunde bachelor and does not name one of the three compulsory study paths. Informatiesystemen most directly continues the mandatory organisational, process and information-system core and the programme’s stated role as a bridge between ICT and organisations. It is therefore selected as the broadest expression of the target’s academic identity, independently of UCR fit.

alternatives.label: Information Systems, Organisations and Digital Society
alternatives.concept: Build programming, database and software development skills. Use research and product design to understand users, and study how organisations adopt technology and make responsible decisions.
alternatives.labelReason: Build programming, database and software development skills. Use research and product design to understand users, and study how organisations adopt technology and make responsible decisions.
progression: Programming precedes databases, software development and advanced algorithms. Introductory data science precedes machine learning and deep learning. Research foundations precede applied statistics and organisational research.

alternatives.label: Data Science and Computational Modelling
alternatives.concept: Build and evaluate statistical and machine learning models. Combine programming and databases with linear algebra, numerical methods and probability, then examine how organisations use data and AI in decisions.
alternatives.labelReason: Build and evaluate statistical and machine learning models. Combine programming and databases with linear algebra, numerical methods and probability, then examine how organisations use data and AI in decisions.
alternatives.distinctness: The data option adds linear algebra, numerical methods, linear systems and probability for a sustained modelling sequence, with Ethics supporting responsible decisions. The closest option emphasises software development, product design, qualitative research, persuasion and organisational behaviour. Each differs by five courses (37.5 EC).
progression: Mathematical Methods precedes linear algebra, numerical methods and probability. Linear algebra precedes Linear Systems and Machine Learning, and Machine Learning precedes deep learning.

alternatives.label: Human Behaviour and Digital Systems
alternatives.concept: Study how people perceive, use and respond to technology. Combine cognition, social psychology and empirical research with product design, digital strategy, AI ethics and the study of institutions.
alternatives.labelReason: Study how people perceive, use and respond to technology. Combine cognition, social psychology and empirical research with product design, digital strategy, AI ethics and the study of institutions.
alternatives.distinctness: The human-centred option adds brain and behaviour, social psychology, perception, cognition, advanced empirical methods and social theory. The closest option emphasises software construction, algorithms and advanced AI. The data option emphasises mathematical and computational modelling. These are different academic progressions as well as different course selections.
progression: Introduction to Brain & Behavior precedes the cognitive-science courses. Social psychology precedes organisational behaviour. Experimental methods precedes advanced research methods, and introductory and modern sociology precede advanced social theory.

selection.assessment: The closest option connects technical system construction with organisational adoption and user research. The data option develops the programme’s data-and-decision interest through mathematical modelling, machine learning and evaluation. The human-centred option develops interests in user needs and social impact through perception, behaviour, research and institutions. The three options each differ from one another by at least four courses. Utrecht’s dedicated UX, process and security courses remain distinct.

blocks: Both develop computational thinking through Python programming.
Both connect the organisation of data to relational databases. UCR covers SQL, normalisation and query processing.
Utrecht brings human communication, visual information and computer-mediated exchange into one course. UCR approaches these areas across courses.
Utrecht has a dedicated course in modelling organisational processes.
Both develop approaches to designing and building software. Utrecht focuses on methods for developing information systems. UCR includes programming, testing and code review.
Utrecht studies how digital services and organisations fit together in an ecosystem.
Utrecht has a dedicated product software course covering the technical and commercial sides of software products.
Utrecht has a dedicated information security course. UCR covers related topics in database authorisation and AI ethics.
Both study organisations and their needs. UCR introduces entrepreneurship and core business functions. Utrecht focuses on how organisations use ICT.
Both examine how organisations use digital technology to pursue strategic goals.
Both use research into user needs to guide design. UCR prototypes consumer products. Utrecht focuses on interactive digital systems.
UCR introduces the brain and behaviour, including foundations for studying cognition. Utrecht has a dedicated course on cognition and emotion.
UCR studies how people perceive and act. Utrecht teaches how to design and evaluate usable digital systems.
Utrecht combines people, society and ICT in one course. UCR studies aspects of that relationship through sociology, business and AI ethics.
Both develop empirical research design and analysis.
UCR develops argument and communication through rhetoric. Utrecht develops academic skills for information science.
Utrecht requires an individual 15 EC project after 120 EC and Scientific Research Methods. UCR’s optional independent research is separate from the scheduled courses.
Utrecht students choose 45 EC of profiling electives, including at least 15 EC at intermediate or advanced level. Choices must avoid overlap with other courses.

notes.text: Utrecht integrates computing, organisations and human interaction through a compulsory core, one defined study path and an individual research project. UCR combines related work across departments. It offers programming, software development, data analysis, design and user research, while Utrecht has dedicated courses in process modelling, digital ecosystems, product software, usability and information security.

audience.programmeDescription: Utrecht’s Information Science bachelor studies how people and organisations design, use and evaluate digital information systems.
audience.comparisonExplanation: This example follows the Information Systems study path. The three UCR options emphasise software and organisations, data modelling, or human behaviour. Utrecht includes specialist courses and a required individual research project.
